clue.text: Quarrel, having gutted fish

indicators.note: to gut a fish is to take out its insides, so the letter at the very centre of the word goes

parts.note: a sprat is a small sea fish

explanation.surface: Two people fall out after one of them has cleaned the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: SPRAT has five letters, so its middle one is the R; remove it and SPAT is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a brief, petty argument, so it works as a noun synonym for a quarrel.

clue.text: In which some are on course for a snap decision?

definitions.text: In which some are on course for a snap decision?

parts.words: In which some are on course for a snap decision?
parts.note: surface reading: people heading towards a hasty judgement made on the spur of the moment

parts.words: In which some are on course for a snap decision?
parts.note: setter's reading: runners on a racecourse whose race is settled by a camera snap at the line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap' suggests haste but means a photograph, and 'course' is a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: When horses or runners cross the line almost together, the result is decided from a photograph taken at the finish.

clue.text: It's assembled haphazardly to assure start of union

definitions.text: It's assembled haphazardly to assure start of union

indicators.note: things put together at random lose their order, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A collection gathered somewhat at random to make sure a marriage gets off to a good start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a bride gathers her outfit and linen ahead of the wedding, the start of a union.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and household linen a bride collects before her marriage begins.

clue.text: Favour European writing in advance

parts.note: to favour something is to be for it
E is the standard abbreviation for European
a hand is a person's handwriting

explanation.surface: A request to prefer European documents that were drafted ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb phrase 'be for' supplies the opening letters, so the answer splits as BE FOR + E + HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Beforehand is an adverb meaning earlier or ahead of time, which is what in advance means.

clue.text: Mistake about old soldiers being ill-mannered

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the words after it

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
O is a standard abbreviation for old
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An error concerning veterans who behaved rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old soldiers' reads as veterans, but it splits into two abbreviations; 'other ranks' is the army term for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Boorish means coarse and rude in behaviour, like a boor, an adjective synonym for ill-mannered.

clue.text: Flighty type first to forfeit freedom, say, on gallows

indicators.note: the first of the following word means just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

indicators.note: say asks for a word as it is spoken, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: liberty is freedom; the spelling here only matches its sound
a gibbet is a gallows from which bodies were hung

explanation.surface: A frivolous person is first to lose their freedom, hanged on the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the gallows word after what comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: A flibbertigibbet is a frivolous, flighty person who chatters too much, a noun matching flighty type.

clue.text: A children's writer's hurried notes

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, to hurry
so and me are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Jottings a children's author scribbled in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of writer's stands for is, joining definition and wordplay. Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons; the A of the clue is his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome is a British author of children's sailing adventures, so he is one children's writer.

clue.text: It's very Italian, failing to complete attack

definitions.note: describes the answer: it is the Italian word for very, used in music

indicators.note: a word that is not completed stops short, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: Something quintessentially Italian that falls short of a full assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very Italian' looks like a description of style; it means the Italian for very, as in the tempo marking allegro assai.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian musical direction meaning very, as in allegro assai, very fast.

clue.text: Energy required for excursion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: determination and ambition, the push to get things done
second meaning: a trip out in a car

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests one needs stamina for an outing; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both inner motivation and vigour and a pleasure journey taken by car.

clue.text: Act of moving cosmetic preparation round Alpine lake

indicators.note: going round something means wrapping about it, so the first word is put on either side of the second

parts.note: a lotion is a cream or liquid put on the skin
Lake Como lies in the Italian Alps

explanation.surface: Someone carrying skin cream around a lake in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is the power or action of moving from place to place, a noun matching the act of moving.

clue.text: Drink contributed to past indiscretions

indicators.note: the answer is something the following words contributed to, a run of letters they supply between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Alcohol played a part in someone's earlier misbehaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from the Piedmont region of Italy, so it is one kind of drink.

clue.text: Japanese shrub, one a climber brought back

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
a social climber, someone who looks up to rank

explanation.surface: A Japanese plant and a mountaineer who has been rescued and returned home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a plant or a mountaineer; here it is the social kind. The whole run I + A + SNOB is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a tree or shrub kept dwarf in a pot by a traditional Japanese method of pruning.

clue.text: Busk in the Tube?

parts.note: surface reading: a street musician performing for coins in the London Underground
setter's reading: to busk is to play, and playing a tube means sounding a pipe with one's breath, which names a hollow tube for shooting darts

explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground railway, where buskers play for change; read as a verb phrase, playing a pipe is what the answer's two halves say.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is literally a tube, and its name splits into blow plus pipe, a way to describe playing a wind instrument.

clue.text: Owl's companion looks down on bat in tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, what looks down on another sits above it, so that piece comes first

parts.note: in Edward Lear's poem The Owl and the Pussy-cat the two go to sea together
cricket bats are made of willow, so the willow is the bat itself

explanation.surface: A cat sitting in a tree peers down at a bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' suggests the flying animal; it is the cricket bat, called the willow after its wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The pussy willow is a small willow whose soft grey catkins look like a cat's fur.

clue.text: Dreadful, to break down crossing river

indicators.note: a road crossing a field runs through its middle, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a car or engine that breaks down is said to die
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a vehicle failing in the middle of a ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire describes something terrible or extremely serious, an adjective synonym for dreadful.

clue.text: African native's social worker in Bret's time

indicators.note: something in a place is enclosed by it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Bret Harte was an American writer of Wild West stories; the possessive keeps the S
the worker bee lives in a social colony
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An African-born welfare officer working in the era of a Western author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a job title; it is the insect, which goes inside HARTE'S before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The hartebeest is a large antelope found only in Africa, so it is a native animal of that continent.

clue.text: Drape flowers round laird regularly in country

indicators.note: the kept letters go in the next word, which holds them

parts.note: a country of the United Kingdom

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Hanging blooms around a Scottish landowner somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' looks like a crossword river, but it belongs to the definition, which is the whole opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To engarland is to adorn or encircle with garlands, which means hanging wreaths of flowers around something.

clue.text: Symbolic fruit with healing properties? Not at first

indicators.note: these words say the opening is absent, so the first letter of the second piece is dropped

parts.note: the fig is a soft, sweet fruit
something curative can cure illness

explanation.surface: A fruit full of meaning that is said to heal, though not straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion applies only to the healing word, not the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative language is metaphorical rather than literal, which means it works through symbols.

clue.text: Loyal friend's current bétes noires

parts.note: AC stands for alternating current
pet hates are one's bêtes noires, the things one cannot stand

explanation.surface: A faithful companion's present pet aversions.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of friend's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid, faithful Achates is Aeneas's companion, so his name became a byword for a loyal friend.

clue.text: Ruler exercises right to divide capital raised

indicators.note: dividing something splits it apart, so the first pieces go inside it
in a down clue a word raised is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the capital of Italy
PE is physical education, school exercises
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sovereign's workouts give him the authority to split the city's funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money; it is a capital city, turned upward and split by the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign ruler of an empire.

clue.text: Portrait painter unknown in the Panaji area

indicators.note: the unknown is inside the region, so its letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: Panaji is the capital of the Indian state of Goa
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A mysterious artist who paints sitters somewhere around Panaji in western India.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya, the Spanish court artist, is famous for his portraits of the royal family.

clue.text: String up in quiet road in Chinese port

indicators.note: one word is in the other, so its letters are wrapped by the word that follows

parts.note: the hushing sound used to ask for quiet
to string someone up is to hang them
the A1, Britain's longest numbered road, written as AI

explanation.surface: Someone is lynched in a quiet street of a Chinese harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; crosswords write the digit 1 as the letter I. The second 'in' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai, on the Yangtze delta, is China's largest city and one of the world's busiest container ports.

clue.text: Like mine, possibly, it's so pleasant out East

indicators.note: out means leaving, so the letter named next is taken away

parts.note: so nice, taken as a phrase
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone says a thing like theirs is very agreeable, apart from somewhere in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like the possessive; it is an explosive mine, and some sea mines are set off by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An acoustic mine is triggered by noise from a ship, so it can be described as sonic.

clue.text: Warning from rebel leader involved in a strike

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

parts.note: taken as written
to lam is to hit hard

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rebel chief who has joined a walkout issues a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action; it means a blow, and the R sits inside that word after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal or sound that alerts people to danger, a noun synonym for warning.

clue.text: Licence to style a woman's hair thus?

parts.note: to perm hair is to style it into lasting waves or curls
the hair, treated this way, is the object of the verb, referred to as it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a hairdresser needs official permission to set a client's hair this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'thus' is the hint: a hairdresser told to perm the hair would say they will perm it.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit is an official document granting permission, so it is a noun synonym for a licence.

clue.text: Make money, making name first; unlikely to spend much?

indicators.note: the letter standing for name is moved from the back to the front while the rest stay in order

parts.note: to earn is to make money by working

explanation.surface: A person who prefers earning a reputation to spending money.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name; only that letter moves, from the end to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is an old-fashioned word for stingy or mean with money, an adjective like unlikely to spend much.

clue.text: Thanks to bishop, new cleaner gets niche in church

parts.note: ta is an informal British word for thanks

indicators.note: something new is made over, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Thanks to a bishop's help, a newly hired church cleaner is given a recess to work in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle can be a canopied recess in a church wall holding an image or the consecrated bread.

clue.text: Print worker's firm may initially be in deprived environment

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word before it, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the next, so the second wraps around the first
an environment is the surroundings, confirming the poor word encloses the other

parts.note: deprived means lacking money
to sit is to be placed somewhere, as a house sits on a hill

explanation.surface: A printing firm's employee may be working in poor conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' is the hard piece: to sit is to be situated, as a house sits on a hill. 'Environment' confirms which word does the surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor is a typesetter, the printing worker who arranges type for pages to be printed.

clue.text: Sound US librarian's description of wet grass

indicators.note: sound tells you to listen to the name rather than read it, taking the word it resembles when spoken

parts.note: Melvil Dewey devised the Dewey Decimal library classification

explanation.surface: A sensible American librarian describing a damp lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' could be an adjective meaning reliable; it is the signal to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass wet with morning moisture is called dewy, the adjective describing it.
